scientific_interpretation: EXP-C-002 provides the stable-correct counterpart to the stable-wrong EXP-C-001 observation. Groq produced zero normalized semantic entropy on both cases, yet one was protected-correct and the other protected-wrong. Therefore semantic stability alone cannot discriminate correctness; it is useful only as one review-trigger signal combined with risk, evidence and independent verification policy.
design_consequences: Do not map zero entropy directly to NO_REVIEW.
Use protected correctness jointly with semantic uncertainty during threshold calibration.
Retain stable-correct and stable-wrong rates separately.
Provider availability must not be mis-scored as reviewer accuracy.
limitations: Only Groq supplied sufficient model samples.
This semantic proxy covers diagnosis classification, not general free-form semantic equivalence.
